 Country Creek Acres Alfalfa Sprouts Recalled For Salmonella
 November 14, 2026 by Linda Larsen 
 Country Creek Acres Alfalfa Sprouts are being recalled for possible Salmonella contamination. Because this recall notice was posted on the FDA’s Enforcement Reports page and not the regular recall page, there is no mention of whether or not any illnesses have been reported to the company to date in connection with the consumption of these seeds or the sprouts made from them. The recalling firm is Country Creek of Weldon Springs, Missouri
 This product was sold to E-commerce customers nationwide. No picture of the recalled product was provided in the recall notice. 
 The recalled item is Country Creek Acres Alfalfa Sprouts Seeds that are packaged in a clear and silver poly bag. There is a white adhesive label on the product along with green, yellow ,and blue lettering. The packages are in 2 ounce, 4 ounce, 8 ounce, and 16 ounce sizes. No code information was provided in the notice. In total, 200 pounds of seeds are included in this recall.
 If you bought any of these seeds, do not eat them and do not sprout them. You can throw them away in a secure garbage can after double bagging them so others can’t see them, or you can take them back to the store where you purchased them for a full refund.
 If you ate these seeds or sprouts or microgreens made from them, monitor your health for the symptoms of Salmonella food poisoning for the next week. If you do get sick, see your doctor.
